description: One-at-a-time mutants (amendment:185-186): each differs from its valid/ parent by exactly one change, verified mechanically by the kill harness rather than asserted here. Each entry also DECLARES that one location in `location`, and test_every_registry_mutant_declares_the_location_it_actually_changes recomputes it from the raw bytes and refuses any disagreement — an earlier revision's M02 prose named the wrong plane and the wrong entry key and nothing noticed, because the harness measured the COUNT of changed locations and never the location itself. `one_change` remains prose describing the NATURE of the edit; `location` is the machine-checked WHERE. The registry is a bijection onto observe_claude_execution.DECISION_IDS — a new decision with no killing mutant fails the build. ladder:286 requires only that each deciding observation has at least one mutation that turns it red; the bijection is this changeset's stricter choice, made because a set equality is mechanically checkable and 'at least one' is not.

kinds.data: the mutant file replaces installs_as inside a throwaway run root; the committed observer runs unchanged over it
kinds.source: a one-hunk unified diff applied to a tmpdir COPY of the observer, never in place, so there is nothing to restore and no restoration journal to corrupt

oracles.reconcile: the committed observer recomputes the decision from the mutated raw bytes
oracles.jsonschema: jsonschema.Draft202012Validator over the closed schema — an external library that shares no code with the observer
oracles.harness_ast: the self-test's own ast walk over the mutated source; it never calls the observer's audit functions

mutants.one_change: add "extra_root_key" at the packet root, a fourth sibling of the three frozen planes

add "extra" inside observation.filesystem.pre.entries["/proof/root"], a path_entry reached only by resolving $ref out of $defs (observation_plane -> filesystem_plane -> inventory -> patternProperties -> path_entry)
mutants.not_equivalent_to: M01 — a root-only-closed copy of the schema rejects M01 and accepts M02. The self-test derives that copy and asserts the disagreement, so the non-equivalence is measured, not claimed.

M03 — a scan of module-level Import nodes passes M04 silently. That is the #1503 shape: a matcher enumerating known members instead of removing a category. The self-test runs a deliberately module-level-only scan and asserts it MISSES M04 while the real scan catches it.

mutants.one_change: copy a candidate-authored verdict field into the observation plane
alter the SHA-256 recorded for one observed settings source
add one undeclared source to the observed set
mutants.not_equivalent_to: M06 — value comparison and membership comparison are different branches; a digest-only check passes M07 untouched.

mutants.one_change: change one tool_use event's tool_use_id so it has no hook lifecycle partner
one hook exits 2 while the stream still reports success
add a post-run path under a legacy absolute root outside every declared writable root
change the post digest of an already-inventoried path outside the declared roots
mutants.not_equivalent_to: M10 — no new path appears, so M10's set difference misses it entirely.

mutants.one_change: record a raw st_mode (0o100600) where stat.S_IMODE truth is 0o600 for a private-root path

location_forms.data: a JSON pointer into the fixture document, or a `lines A-B: <opcode>` range for the line-oriented .jsonl and .log parents
location_forms.source: the unified-diff hunk header of the single hunk, with its added/removed line counts appended — so a hunk that moves because the observer's bytes shifted turns the check red
